import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Fill missing 'Sleep Disorder' values with 'None' for better categorical plotting
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep
# Use BMI Category for color, Stress Level for marker size, and Sleep Disorder for marker style
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',          # Color points based on BMI Category
    size='Stress Level',         # Size points based on Stress Level
    sizes=(100, 800),            # Adjust the range of marker sizes
    style='Sleep Disorder',      # Use different markers for Sleep Disorder
    palette='viridis',           # Choose a color palette
    alpha=0.8                    # Set transparency for points
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by BMI, Stress, and Sleep Disorder', fontsize=18)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
# Seaborn automatically generates multiple legends for hue, size, and style.
# Adjust layout to prevent legends from overlapping with the plot.
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as output.png
plt.savefig('output.png')
